title: External AI review: redact a pack, get a vendor verdict, never auto-apply (ADR-0009)
body:
NPDev can delegate a human-judgment step to an external AI model under governance: redacted pack in -> vendor -> structured verdict out -> filed, never auto-applied. Two model-level fields opt an app into this: a field-level `sensitive: true` flag (marks a field for redaction before any pack may include it), and an app-level `externalAi` block: `{"egress": "denied"|"packOnly"|"apiEnabled", "vendors": ["openai"]}`. `egress` defaults to `denied` -- nothing leaves any app until an author opts in. Setting `egress` to anything but `denied` with an empty/missing `vendors` list is a SemanticValidator error ("externalAi.egress is 'X' but no vendors are declared"); declare at least one vendor id.

Surfaces: a ControlPanel page at `/api/admin/review/view` (SUPERUSER-gated) with `/pack` (build, no egress), `/submit` (the actual publish action), and `/ingest` (record a verdict) REST endpoints; a CLI (`npdev review pack --mission-id X` / `npdev review ingest --mission-id X --vendor-id Y --verdict-file Z`); and MCP tools `npdev_build_review_pack` / `npdev_ingest_review_verdict`.

Honesty rules enforced structurally, not just by convention: a verdict's `recordKind` is always the literal `external-ai-verdict` -- never `independent-human-review`, never a sign-off. `noRepoAccess` is always `true` and `autoApplied` is always `false` (both are `const`-locked in `external-ai-verdict.schema.json`). Findings are filed, never auto-applied. Ingesting a verdict that fails any of these three checks is a hard error, not a warning.

The pack producer exists in two implementations that must agree byte-for-byte on `manifestSha256` for the same input: the platform's git-pinned Python script (`scripts/external-review/build-review-pack.py`, used for NPDev's own missions) and the product's Java `ReviewPackBuilder` (`com.npdev.adapters.externalai.packcore`, used by a generated app's own ControlPanel). Both compute the manifest hash over canonical (sorted-key, no-whitespace) JSON excluding the wall-clock `generatedAt` field, so two builds of identical input always hash identically -- this is what a run record's `packManifestSha256` proves it is about.

See `docs/adr/ADR-0009-external-ai-delegation.md` for the full governance model (what this does and does not close: never E5 real participants, E6 checkpoint/repo authority, or E7 owner policy decisions).
